PRJNA1524548 ITS2 reruns (Šlapeta group, unpublished)

The 82 ITS2 runs of PRJNA1524548 (Šlapeta group, University of Sydney; unpublished): cultured larvae from cattle, plus faecal samples from kangaroos, pigs and rabbits, each sample as two libraries. Sequenced 2x251, trimmed with bin/trim_primers.py, denoised once with DADA2 and joined three ways, plus the same reads cut to 2x150. Classified against this database (nemits2 v0.1.1 with the 2026-11-11 curation pass) and the nemabiome backbone.

  • The gap rule names 95.2–95.9% of reads to species (hybrid, merged, 2x150) against 68–74% for the published method (assignTaxonomy on nemabiome). Most of the gain is Haemonchus: nemabiome leaves 19–25% of reads at genus, this database names them H. placei.
  • No classifier pair disagrees at species on any set: where two both name a species it is the same one.
  • Half the libraries have read 2 starting inside 28S, with no NC2 primer (49% of read pairs). A trim that requires NC2 throws them away; trimming at the conserved 28S motif keeps them, so all 82 runs count instead of about 41, and 93.9% of read pairs pass. Chimera removal now drops 0.6% of reads, from 1.7%.
  • Merging loses the pig lungworm. Metastrongylus apri ITS2 is 413–422 bases, too long for 2x250 pairs to overlap. Two of the four pig libraries keep 6 and 665 reads merged against 22,932 and 19,801 with hybrid joining; across the set M. apri rises from 1.6% to 3.0% of reads.
  • Hybrid joining gets this at no cost to the calls (gap rule 95.2% hybrid, 95.7% merged). Concatenating every pair drops it to 69%: the short Oesophagostomum radiatum ITS2 is read through by read 1, and scoring the two reads as separate windows charges the overrun into 28S. The k-mer classifiers on 28S-cut ASVs name 99% of concatenated reads.
  • Where the gap rule still stops at genus (about 4% of hybrid reads): Oesophagostomum variants under 99% to any record (2.4%), and kangaroo Cloacina, a dense genus of close species (0.9%). Cooperia, which stopped at genus before, is now named (C. punctata 1.5%, C. oncophora 1.1%), since the curation pass folded the male morphs C. spatulata and C. surnabada into them.
